Last month, after the TV tracking app TV Time officially shut down, its co-founder Antonio Pinto immediately announced the launch of a brand-new film and TV tracking app called Bingers, which will place greater emphasis on social features. Below is the full story.

Bingers is now available for download

When Whip Media announced the closure of TV Time, one of its co-founding executives immediately announced the launch of Bingers, positioning it as "a fast and beautiful wishlist paired with a fun and engaging community."

According to TechCrunch's exclusive report, Bingers is now available for download on iOS and Android, offering a sense of continuity for users who have long been searching for an alternative — after all, TV Time was once one of the world's most popular TV tracking apps.

Users who saved their data through TV Time's export tool before it shut down can import their libraries into Bingers for a seamless transition; as for users who never exported their data, or newcomers using a TV tracking app for the first time, they can start building their own watch records from scratch.

Bingers has significantly strengthened its community-driven features, including user profiles, reviews, show ratings, GIFs, polls, and character popularity battles. Pinto told TechCrunch that these were precisely the key elements that had made TV Time so beloved by users over the years:

For users who simply want to keep track of the TV shows and movies they've watched, Bingers offers standalone wishlist and watch-tracking features. Similar to TV Time, the app also displays a calendar of upcoming broadcast and premiere dates, with a countdown function showing how many days remain until each show's premiere.

Bingers is now available for free download on the App Store, and currently offers no in-app purchases.
